  "text": "Every Thursday, a fresh egg appeared in the locked drawer of Daniel’s desk.

He worked on the seventh floor of an insurance office. There were no birds nearby, unless you counted the pigeons sulking beneath the station roof.

The first egg he threw away. The second he carried home in a paper cup. By the fourth Thursday, he had stopped mentioning them to his colleagues.

They were small, pale green, and warm.

One morning he found a crack running around the shell. Something inside knocked three times.

Daniel shut the drawer.

His mother used to knock that way on his bedroom door: two quick taps, then one after a pause. She had been dead eleven years.

He opened the drawer again.

The egg lay beside his stapler. A flake of shell had fallen away, revealing darkness and the smell of toast.

He leaned closer.

Somewhere inside, a radio played the shipping forecast. A spoon struck the side of a cup.

“Nearly ready,” his mother called.

Daniel sat very still until someone asked whether he wanted lunch.

That evening, he wrapped the egg in his scarf and took the bus home. He cleared the kitchen table, set out a saucer, and waited.

By midnight, the crack had widened enough to show a strip of yellow wallpaper.

He fetched a teaspoon, then put it back.

In the morning, there was only an empty shell.

Daniel searched beneath the table and behind the fridge. At last he noticed the toast on his plate, cut into triangles, and a small thumbprint of butter on the knife."
